guitar.notes: Tom Scholz is known for Gibson Les Pauls run through his own Rockman gear; fairly well known but not as singularly iconic as e.g. Slash's, so medium fits.

tone.target: bright compressed Boston lead with smooth sustain
tone.profile: bright compressed Boston lead with smooth sustain
tone.summary: A clean/slightly driven signal chain utilizing compression for sustain, a Boost for added girth, an AC30-style amp for brightness, Chorus for sheen, and Plate reverb for smooth ambience.
corrections: keep lead tone more saturated than clean

rig.name: Boston - Peace Of Mind - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide smooth sustain and even out dynamics for lead lines.
Add girth and lift the signal for lead playing without heavy crunch.
Provide subtle saturation and grit to the lead tone, keeping it bright.
blocks.gap: The Red Haze is used here for controlled breakup rather than heavy distortion, matching the 'saturated but not crunchy' requirement.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the bright, articulate British tone associated with classic pop-rock leads.
Provide a classic British voicing that complements the AC30 model.
Add the required 'sheen' and width to the lead tone.
Enhance the upper mids and brightness for clarity and presence.
Provide smooth, controlled ambience without sounding washy.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for better upper-mid articulation and sustain.

proposals.recommendedAsset: song-appropriate IR (e.g., Celestion Greenback or similar)
proposals.reason: Enhance upper mids and articulate the lead tone better than the generic UK Vintage 4x12.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and definition in the high end.
